import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t_task = np.linspace(0, 1, 500)  # start from the time axis the Seed provides

clips.caption: First prepare a uniform <emphasis level="strong">time axis</emphasis> from 0 to 1 second.

actions.text:
low = 0.8 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 1.0 * t_task + np.pi / 4)  # low frequency component: 1 Hz, amplitude 0.8
high = 0.3 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 4.0 * t_task)  # high frequency component: 4 Hz, amplitude 0.3
x_task = low + high  # a low and a high frequency component added together

clips.caption: A low <emphasis level="strong">frequency</emphasis> component at 1 Hz with <emphasis level="strong">amplitude</emphasis> 0.8 and a π/4 <emphasis level="strong">phase</emphasis>; a high frequency component at 4 Hz with amplitude 0.3; add them sample by sample.

actions.text:
plt.figure(figsize=(7, 3))
plt.plot(t_task, low, label="low: 1 Hz, A=0.8, phase=pi/4")
plt.plot(t_task, high, label="high: 4 Hz, A=0.3")
plt.plot(t_task, x_task, label="sum")
plt.title("A signal with low and high frequency components")
plt.xlabel("Time (s)")
plt.ylabel("Amplitude")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

clips.caption: Draw both components and the combined <emphasis level="strong">signal</emphasis> and check whether the high <emphasis level="strong">frequency</emphasis> detail rides on the low frequency swing.
